title: Storyboard uses hypothesis and MVN uses actual frames

stages.invocation: Mode: Best guess. SYNTHETIC teaching case. Target: maintenance managers in mid-sized manufacturing plants. Selected concept: report comparison. Human-selected hypothesis: making source/recency visible may help a person explain the next investigation. Task: compare fictional reports and explain next action and uncertainty. Decision rule: revise if context confuses; explore coordination if permission dominates; another bounded test if reasoning becomes clearer. No MVN exists yet. Create the six descriptive frames and a renderer prompt if useful; no rendering.

Mode: Best guess. SYNTHETIC. Use only the actual storyboard handoff to write the six-part MVN and prototype-ready descriptive prompt. Preserve hypothesis, task and rule. Do not render, build or invent missing frames. Stop at the human gate.

gate_reply: Scripted teaching choice: approve these fictional frames for narrative work only. Carry the actual six frames, hypothesis, task, uncertainty and rule in the handoff. No rendering or participant test has run. Stop.

criteria.rule: Storyboard develops six descriptive frames directly from hypothesis; it does not require a preexisting MVN or silently render.
MVN uses the actual prior six frames and preserves actor agency, hypothesis and rule; no new unselected solution or missing frame invented.
